methods.label: Track odd and even results
methods.explanation:
Use the usual fair-spinner interpretation, with the three sectors of \(P\) equally likely. Since we only need to know whether the sum is odd, track odd and even results rather than every possible sum.

Every number on \(Q\) is even, and every number on \(R\) is odd. Their sum is therefore always odd. Adding an even result from \(P\) keeps the total odd, while adding an odd result makes the total even.

Of \(P\)'s labels \(1,2,3\), only \(2\) is even. Exactly one of its three equally likely sectors works, so the probability is \(\boxed{\frac13}\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
methods.levelReason: Odd-even addition reduces the problem to counting one favorable sector out of three equally likely sectors, within AMC 8 probability.

candidate.annotationRationale: The task assesses a simple equally likely probability. The written method uses odd-even reasoning to reduce the event to one spinner, then expresses favorable sectors as a fraction of all sectors. It does not use independence or enumerate three-spinner outcomes.
limitations: The numerical probability uses the usual fair-spinner interpretation that P's three sectors are equally likely. Independence among the three spinners is not needed.
